\section[abhinandanegaḷu]{\kn{ಅಭಿನಂದನೆಗಳು} (abhinandanegaḷu) — congratulations}

\label{lesson:KA-C88-congratulations}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for is that so, then the Kannada for the same.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಅಭಿನಂದನೆಗಳು}}
\textbf{\kn{ಅಭಿನಂದನೆಗಳು}} (\emph{abhinandanegaḷu}) — \textquotedblleft{}congratulations\textquotedblright{}. The ending \textbf{‑\kn{ಗಳು}} (\emph{-gaḷu}) is the plural: many good wishes.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Good news deserves a word of its own.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{abhinandanegaḷu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{abhinandanegaḷu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{abhinandanegaḷu!}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for is that so, then the Kannada for the same, then say \emph{abhinandanegaḷu} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಅಭಿನಂದನೆಗಳು} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Congratulations\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[āhvāna]{\kn{ಆಹ್ವಾನ} (āhvāna) — an invitation}

\label{lesson:KA-C88-invitation}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for the same, then the Kannada for congratulations.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಆಹ್ವಾನ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಆಹ್ವಾನ}} (\emph{āhvāna}) — \textquotedblleft{}an invitation\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\kn{ನಿಮಗೆ} \kn{ಆಹ್ವಾನ}} (\emph{nimage āhvāna}) — \textquotedblleft{}an invitation for you\textquotedblright{}, with \textbf{\kn{ನಿಮಗೆ}}, \textquotedblleft{}to you\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
How a celebration begins.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āhvāna}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āhvāna}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{nimage āhvāna}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for the same, then the Kannada for congratulations, then say \emph{āhvāna} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಆಹ್ವಾನ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An invitation\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[uḍugore]{\kn{ಉಡುಗೊರೆ} (uḍugore) — a gift}

\label{lesson:KA-C88-gift}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for congratulations, then the Kannada for an invitation.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಉಡುಗೊರೆ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಉಡುಗೊರೆ}} (\emph{uḍugore}) — \textquotedblleft{}a gift, a present\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\kn{ನಿಮಗೆ} \kn{ಒಂದು} \kn{ಉಡುಗೊರೆ}} (\emph{nimage ondu uḍugore}) — \textquotedblleft{}a gift for you\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
What you bring to the celebration.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{uḍugore}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{uḍugore}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{nimage ondu uḍugore}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for congratulations, then the Kannada for an invitation, then say \emph{uḍugore} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಉಡುಗೊರೆ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A gift\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[oḷage banni]{\kn{ಒಳಗೆ} \kn{ಬನ್ನಿ} (oḷage banni) — please come in}

\label{lesson:KA-C88-comein}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for an invitation, then the Kannada for a gift.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಒಳಗೆ} \kn{ಬನ್ನಿ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಒಳಗೆ} \kn{ಬನ್ನಿ}} (\emph{oḷage banni}) — \textquotedblleft{}please come in\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{\kn{ಒಳಗೆ}} is \textquotedblleft{}inside\textquotedblright{}, and \textbf{\kn{ಬನ್ನಿ}} is the polite form of \textbf{\kn{ಬಾ}}, \textquotedblleft{}come\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The first thing said at the door.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{oḷage banni}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{oḷage banni}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{oḷage banni}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for an invitation, then the Kannada for a gift, then say \emph{oḷage banni} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಒಳಗೆ} \kn{ಬನ್ನಿ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Please come in\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[svāgata]{\kn{ಸ್ವಾಗತ} (svāgata) — welcome}

\label{lesson:KA-C88-welcome}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for a gift, then the Kannada for come in.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಸ್ವಾಗತ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಸ್ವಾಗತ}} (\emph{svāgata}) — \textquotedblleft{}welcome\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\kn{ನಿಮಗೆ} \kn{ಸ್ವಾಗತ}} (\emph{nimage svāgata}) — \textquotedblleft{}welcome to you\textquotedblright{}, the formal greeting on a signboard or at a door.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The formal greeting for a guest.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{svāgata}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{nimage svāgata}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for a gift, then the Kannada for come in, then say \emph{svāgata} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
